question: The audible frequency range of hearing for an average human beings is from about:
solution:
The correct answer is __**20 Hz to 20 kHz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The average human ear can hear sounds in the frequency range of **20 Hz to 20 kHz**.
 
• Frequencies below 20 Hz are known as **infrasound**, and those above 20 kHz are termed as **ultrasound**.
 
• This range is also referred to as the **audible range** or the range of human hearing.
 
• The sensitivity of human hearing varies within this range, being most sensitive between **2 kHz and 5 kHz**, where speech frequencies are concentrated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrasound**

 
 
• Infrasound refers to sound waves with frequencies below the lower limit of human audibility, generally below 20 Hz.
 
• Infrasound can be produced by natural sources such as earthquakes, volcanoes, and severe weather, as well as by man-made sources like engines and explosions.
 
 
 
• **Ultrasound**
 
 
• Ultrasound refers to sound waves with frequencies above the upper limit of human hearing, above 20 kHz.
 
• Ultrasound is widely used in medical imaging, industrial nondestructive testing, and cleaning.
 
 
 
• **Hearing Sensitivity**
 
 
• Human hearing is not equally sensitive across all frequencies; it is most sensitive in the range of 2 kHz to 5 kHz.
 
• This range is important for understanding speech, which is why many hearing tests focus on these frequencies.
 
 
 
• **Hearing Loss**
 
 
• Exposure to very loud sounds or prolonged exposure to high noise levels can cause hearing loss, particularly at higher frequencies.
 
• Regular hearing tests are important for detecting and managing hearing loss early.
